newsitem.title: UK: NAPF calls tax credit cut attack' on UK pensions.
newsitem.headline: NAPF calls tax credit cut attack' on UK pensions.

text.p: Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon Brown's Wednesday abolition of the Advanced Corporation Tax (ACT) credit is "the biggest attack on funded pension provision since the war," according to the National Association of Pension Funds (NAPF).
"This measure will take over 50 billion stg of extra pension contributions from public and private sector employees over the next ten years," said NAPF chairman Peter Murray in a statement.
Brown abolished the ACT credit, which allows tax-exempt institutions such as pension funds to claim back the 20 percent ACT, thereby making UK equity holdings more attractive.
"Local authorities will have to put up council taxes, cut services and lay off workers to ensure that pensions are properly funded," Murray said.

"Tomorrow morning all over the UK, finance directors of UK companies and all those people with money purchase schemes and personal pensions will wake up to find that their pensions will be a lot smaller unless they pump in more contributions," Murray said.
